title: Symmetric energy over a powerset
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ whose constant-one element is indexed by $0$ and which is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product. For a positive integer $n$, let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$ be invariant under every permutation of its coordinates, and let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The sum of the energies of the orthogonal components indexed by the nonempty subsets of $S$ equals $\sum_{k=0}^{|S|}\binom{|S|}{k} E_k$, where $E_0=0$ and, for $k>0$, $E_k$ is the energy of the component indexed by the first $k$ coordinates.
